transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Javier Ortega (CTO - Cygnus), Maya Lin (ML Lead), Samir Patel (PM)

Summary (auto): Focus on model/context needs, multilingual, tool-calling, deployment options and security. Next: pricing, pilot, security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining last call of the year, appreciate it. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya's our SE, she'll walk through model tradeoffs. Javier, Maya, Samir, you all good to go?
[00:18] Javier Ortega: Yep, thanks Alex. Happy to be here. Quick context: Cygnus is building a docs + chat assistant for enterprise customers, we need very long context windows — think entire contract bundles, legal docs, internal knowledge bases.
[00:30] Maya Lin: and we need support for ES, FR, JP and some Portuguese, also tool-calling to query our internal DBs and run calculated fields.
[00:45] Priya Desai: great, that's helpful. Quick question on scale — what concurrency are you expecting during peak?
[00:52] Samir Patel: ballpark 40-60 concurrent chat sessions, spikes to ~120 for scheduled batch ingests. Latency SLO target is p95 under 350ms if possible. Cost is also a big factor though — want predictable bill.
[01:10] Priya Desai: understood. For 100k token context you basically have two levers: model that natively supports long context (128k variants) or use RAG + chunking. For open models, some LLMs in our catalog hit 128k with quantized tails but there's a cost/latency hit.
[01:32] Maya Lin: when you say "in our catalog" — are we talking Redwood-hosted open weights or managed OpenAI/Anthropic?
[01:38] Alex Monroe: primarily hosted open models and our curated variants, we also support Anthropic/OpenAI as fallbacks in routing policies. We can run on Hosted for eval and then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation, or Private for full on-prem/vpc.
[01:55] Priya Desai: just to add, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better latency consistency; Private is for customers who need on-prem or air-gapped. Hosted is fastest to get started. Tradeoffs: cost, control, and compliance.
[02:15] Javier Ortega: security is huge for us — SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, ability to run in our VPC. Also need to keep data residency in EU. Does Redwood support customer KMS and HSM?
[02:25] Priya Desai: yes — we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers and can support customer-managed keys for Private or Dedicated with the right contract. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the console; we'll share the SOC2 pack after this meeting.
[02:42] Samir Patel: perfect. On model quality — we run some domain-specific legal QA; how do you recommend balancing open model choice and finetuning/quantization to keep cost down?
[02:52] Priya Desai: common pattern is choose a base open model with good long-context behavior, apply quantization (4-bit/ggml style) and then do light instruction-tuning or retrieval. Often Dedicated can enable cheaper per-token cost due to reserved capacity; also caching prefixes and KV cache helps a lot for repeated contexts.
[03:15] Maya Lin: we were worried about function-calling — we need models to reliably trigger tool calls with structured outputs. Any support there?
[03:22] Priya Desai: yes — our runtime supports function/tool calling and structured output. There's sometimes transcription of the tool name in logs (heh) but function schemas are supported and you can wire to your internal APIs. We'll demo that in the SE follow-up.
[03:36] Alex Monroe: to be concrete, what are your must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
[03:40] Javier Ortega: must-haves: EU data residency, KMS customer keys, long context >=100k tokens (or equivalent RAG with no quality loss), tool-calling reliability, reasonable latency p95 <350ms for interactive flows. Nice-to-haves: cheaper cost per 1M tokens, multi-region redundancy.
[03:59] Priya Desai: good list. For the 100k context — we should validate with a benchmark. Our suggestion: run a pilot where we serve a 100k doc, measure p95, and compare pure long-context model vs RAG hybrid.
[04:15] Samir Patel: how long for pilot and what's the expected cost?
[04:19] Alex Monroe: pilot typically 2 weeks: initial ingest/tests + perf runs. Cost depends on model and deployment mode; we'll give Hosted estimate for quick test and Dedicated for production pricing.
[04:30] Maya Lin: one more question — multilingual quality often drops on some open models; do you have specific model recommendations?
[04:36] Priya Desai: yes — there are a couple of community models we surface that have stronger multilingual alignment; we also suggest tiny instruction-tuning or use a translation fallback for low-resource languages. We'll include recommended model list in the follow-up.
[04:50] Javier Ortega: competitor question — we've looked at Anthropic for safety and OpenAI for tool-support. Where does Redwood fit if we want both control and model capabilities?
[04:59] Alex Monroe: Redwood is deployment & runtime-first: we let you pick the model and give consistent serving primitives — batching, KV cache, tool-calling, rollout controls. If you need control + compliance, Dedicated or Private is the path, but you can start Hosted to iterate.
[05:16] Priya Desai: small note on perf — we'll test sequence length distribution. For 100k documents if tokens are sparse (lots of text), we can chunk; if you need true single-context attention, the 128k-capable variants will be more costly.
[05:33] Maya Lin: okay, what do you need from us to get the benchmark started?
[05:37] Priya Desai: sample documents, language list, expected concurrency, success criteria (latency p95 target, cost per 1M tokens threshold), and any security requirements (KMS, regions).
[05:50] Samir Patel: we'll provide samples and do a short internal review with security.
[05:55] Alex Monroe: we'll also put together a pilot proposal with Hosted + Dedicated cost lines. Expect pricing doc from me by Jan 5. Priya will send the benchmark repo and instructions.
[06:05] Javier Ortega: sounds good. One more nit — auditability: how easy is it to pull per-request logs for compliance purposes?
[06:12] Priya Desai: console exports and API access; we can generate logs with request/response hashes and policy metadata. For Private you can retain everything internally. We'll share the audit log schema.
[06:26] Maya Lin: any gotchas about on-prem / private deployment?
[06:29] Priya Desai: the usual: longer lead time, packaging & infra requirements, and there are sizing discussions — e.g., for 100k contexts you'll need GPU configurations that handle the KV and memory. We'll map that out in the follow-up.
[06:44] Samir Patel: are there known open-models with 128k that you recommend?
[06:48] Priya Desai: there are several community variants; we'll send a curated list (we had a doc with per-model perf and multilingual notes). Some names may be transcribed weird in the meeting (sorry) but we'll give the canonical names/links.
[07:05] Alex Monroe: ok let's recap action items and next steps...
[07:10] Alex Monroe: Alex -> pricing and pilot proposal by 2027-01-05; Priya -> benchmark script and README by 2027-01-07; Maya -> sample docs and language list by 2027-01-04; Javier -> security checklist confirmations by 2027-01-06. We'll follow up with a SE-led deep dive the week of Jan 11.
[07:32] Javier Ortega: all good, thanks everyone. Happy new year early.
[07:35] Maya Lin: thanks, bye.
[07:37] Alex Monroe: thanks all, bye.
